partner_context.their_ambition: Washington State Ferries is the largest ferry system in the United States, carrying ~20M+ riders a year across Puget Sound, under a state mandate to electrify its aging diesel fleet.
partner_context.their_pressure: The car-ferry fleet is aging and capacity-constrained, electrification is costly and slow, and fast passenger-only demand (King County Water Taxi, Kitsap Fast Ferries) keeps outgrowing supply — while Puget Sound road and bridge congestion worsens.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling passenger fleet that adds fast, clean, low-wake connections across the Sound — supplementing the car ferries, expanding fast passenger service, and advancing the electrification mandate without new shoreside infrastructure.

hero.title: The Puget Sound fast-water layer.
hero.subtitle: Foiling passenger service that extends the nation's largest ferry system — clean, fast, low-wake.
hero.what_we_do_together: Washington State Ferries and the region's transit agencies bring the routes, ridership and electrification mandate; Navier brings a foiling passenger fleet that adds fast new water connections without new roads or bridges — and helps decarbonize the fleet.

why_now: Washington has legislated the electrification of its ferry fleet, fast passenger-only ridership is at record highs, and Puget Sound's bridges and highways are gridlocked — the moment for a clean foiling passenger layer is now.
multimodal_fit: Puget Sound commuters already mix bus, light rail and ferry; a foiling passenger pier slots into the same trip — light rail to the waterfront, foil across the Sound, transit onward — adding fast water capacity to the regional network.

journeys_unlocked.today: A ~60-min car ferry or a Kitsap fast ferry at capacity.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast clean foiling passenger crossing of the Sound — frequent, low-wake, electric.

journeys_unlocked.today: A congested car-ferry crossing with long vehicle queues.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A frequent foiling passenger service that skips the vehicle queue entirely.

journeys_unlocked.today: A long, infrequent car ferry through the islands.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast clean Quanta-LR hybrid passenger run through the San Juans — no charging dependence on remote islands.

journeys_unlocked.today: No direct fast water service today.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A clean Quanta-LR hybrid line-haul down the length of Puget Sound.

differentiation.why_navier: A software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling passenger platform that adds fast clean capacity with only a berth pedestal — advancing the electrification mandate without the cost and timeline of re-powering car ferries, and with far lower wake on sensitive Sound shorelines.

proof_points.claim: WSF is the largest US ferry system.
proof_points.evidence: ~20M+ annual riders across Puget Sound on an aging, capacity-constrained car-ferry fleet.
A state mandate to electrify the ferry fleet creates direct policy alignment for zero-emission foiling vessels.
King County Water Taxi and Kitsap Fast Ferries run at capacity, with constant pressure to expand routes.
Puget Sound bridges and highways are gridlocked, with the water the only uncongested right-of-way.

objections.concern: WSF runs car ferries; foiling is passenger-only.
objections.response: Correct — Navier supplements rather than replaces the car ferries, adding fast passenger capacity on congested corridors and new routes the car fleet can't economically serve.

objections.concern: Puget Sound has heavy weather and commercial traffic.
objections.response: Foils ride above the chop; software-defined routing flexes with conditions and manages traffic separation, and the Sound is largely sheltered.

objections.concern: Procurement is slow and politically scrutinized.
objections.response: We start with a regional fast-ferry pilot (King County / Kitsap) to prove the model before any WSF fleet decision — de-risking the path.

objections.concern: Marine-mammal and wake rules are strict.
objections.response: Zero-wake foiling is far gentler on shorelines and orca habitat than planing craft — an environmental advantage, not a hurdle.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Cross-Sound fast passenger pilot (Pioneer II)
phases.narrative: Launch a foiling passenger pilot on the busiest cross-Sound corridors — Seattle↔Bremerton and Seattle↔Bainbridge/Kingston — proving fast, clean, low-wake capacity that skips the car-ferry vehicle queues.
phases.rationale: Highest-demand corridors with proven fast-ferry ridership.

phases.label: Phase 2 — San Juan Islands + South Sound (Quanta-LR)
phases.narrative: Add Quanta-LR hybrid passenger service through the San Juan Islands and down the length of Puget Sound to Olympia — clean range with no charging dependence on remote islands.
phases.rationale: Long routes the car fleet serves slowly and infrequently.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Regional foiling passenger network
phases.narrative: Scale to a regional foiling passenger network integrated with WSF, light rail and bus — the fast clean water layer of Puget Sound transit, advancing the electrification mandate.
phases.rationale: A clean, fast water layer for the whole Sound.

the_ask.navier_brings: The foiling passenger fleet, captain training, maintenance and certification path, and the software-defined operating platform.
the_ask.partner_brings: WSF and regional agencies bring the routes, terminals, ridership base, electrification mandate and public-transit integration.
the_ask.together: A fast, clean, low-wake foiling passenger layer that extends the nation's largest ferry system and advances its electrification goals.

close.title: Puget Sound, faster and cleaner.
close.body: A foiling passenger layer that adds fast clean capacity across the Sound — supplementing the car ferries, expanding fast service, and advancing the electrification mandate without new infrastructure.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Washington's ferry-electrification mandate, record fast-ferry ridership, and worsening cross-Sound road congestion converge — a foiling passenger fleet delivers clean fast capacity now.

end_state.headline: The fast, clean water layer of Puget Sound transit.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Seattle + Bremerton + Bainbridge + Kingston + Anacortes/San Juans + South Sound (Olympia/Tacoma).
end_state.narrative: A foiling passenger network runs across Puget Sound integrated with WSF, light rail and bus — fast, clean, low-wake capacity that skips the car-ferry queues, serves the islands cleanly, and advances Washington's electrification mandate.
